papers.title: Robust Reduced-Order Model Stabilization for Partial Differential Equations Based on Lyapunov Theory and Extremum Seeking with Application to the 3D Boussinesq Equations
papers.abstract: We present some results on stabilization for reduced-order models (ROMs) of partial differential equations. The stabilization is achieved using Lyapunov theory to design a new closure model that is robust to parametric uncertainties. The free parameters in the proposed ROM stabilization method are optimized using a model-free multi-parametric extremum seeking (MES) algorithm. The 3D Boussinesq equations provide a challenging numerical test-problem that is used to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的降阶模型稳定化方法在参数不确定性下具有鲁棒性，可迁移到生物力学代理模型设计，但未涉及植入物或固体力学验证。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address biomedical implants, solid mechanics, or experimental validation; it focuses solely on fluid dynamics PDEs (3D Boussinesq equations).

summary_zh.result: 在三维Boussinesq方程上验证了稳定性和鲁棒性提升。
summary_zh.validation: 三维Boussinesq方程数值测试问题。

summary_en.motivation: Develop a robust reduced-order model (ROM) stabilization method for partial differential equations under parametric uncertainty.
summary_en.method: Use Lyapunov theory to design a closure model and optimize its free parameters with a model-free multi-parametric extremum seeking algorithm.
summary_en.result: The method enhances stability and robustness, demonstrated on the 3D Boussinesq equations.
summary_en.validation: Numerical simulation on a challenging test problem of 3D Boussinesq equations.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the fatigue behavior of type 630 stainless steel fabricated by selective laser melting, focusing on the role of process-induced defects.
summary_en.method: Fatigue tests were conducted on SLM 630 stainless steel specimens, and fracture surfaces were analyzed to correlate defect characteristics with fatigue life.
summary_en.result: Fatigue life is dominated by defects; process parameters and post-treatment significantly affect fatigue performance.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fatigue data from multiple specimen batches were compared to validate the defect-dependence mechanism.

papers.title: Biologically Inspired Smart Release System Based on 3D Bioprinted Perfused Scaffold for Vascularized Tissue Regeneration
papers.abstract: A critical challenge to the development of large-scale artificial tissue grafts for defect reconstruction is vascularization of the tissue construct. As an emerging tissue/organ manufacturing technique, 3D bioprinting offers great precision in controlling the internal architecture of a scaffold with preferable mechanical strength and printing complicated microstructures comparable to native tissue. However, current bioprinting techniques still exhibit difficulty in achieving biomimetic nano resolution and cooperating with bioactive spatiotemporal signals. In this study, a comprehensive design of engineered vascularized bone construct is presented for the first time by integrating biomimetic 3D bioprinted fluid perfused microstructure with biologically inspired smart release nanocoating, which is regarded as an aspiring concept combining engineering, biological, and material science. In this biologically inspired design, angiogenesis and osteogenesis are successively induced through a matrix metalloprotease 2 regulative mechanism by delivering dual growth factors with sequential release in spatiotemporal coordination. Availability of this system is evaluated in dynamic culture condition, which is similar to fluid surrounding in vivo, as an alternative animal model study. Results, particularly from co-cultured dynamically samples demonstrate excellent bioactivity and vascularized bone forming potential of nanocoating modified 3D bioprinted scaffolds for human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and human umbilical vein endothelial cells.

papers.title: The prospects for additive manufacturing of bulk TiAl alloy
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the prospects for additive manufacturing (AM) of bulk TiAl alloys. A number of AM processes have already been explored in the literature for these intermetallic alloys. The main trend developed in published works concerns a strong crack sensitivity of this relatively brittle material due to rapid successive heating and cooling cycles. Optimised processing conditions have already been achieved for producing sound and crack-free TiAl materials by means of EBM and laser metal deposition processes. This experimental work was particularly focused on the third process, i.e. selective laser melting, to produce fully dense TiAl parts. A series of beads, surface layers and cubes have been manufactured to investigate the microstructural evolution. Post-heat treatments allowed a uniform microstructure to be restored for the intermetallic TiAl alloy.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是TiAl合金的增材制造工艺，与生物医学植入物无关，未涉及应力遮挡、多孔结构或骨整合等方向的核心问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on TiAl intermetallic alloy processing for high-temperature applications, with no biomedical context, no porous structures, no stress shielding analysis, no mechanical testing for implants, and no osseointegration or surface roughness considerations.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索TiAl合金的增材制造可行性及裂纹控制。
summary_zh.method: 采用SLM、EBM和激光沉积工艺制备TiAl样品并表征微观组织。
summary_zh.result: 优化工艺可获无裂纹致密TiAl材料，后热处理可恢复均匀组织。
summary_zh.validation: 通过金相和微观组织观察验证工艺效果。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the processability of crack-sensitive TiAl intermetallic alloys using additive manufacturing techniques.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting, electron beam melting, and laser metal deposition were employed to fabricate TiAl beads, layers, and cubes, followed by microstructural characterization.
summary_en.result: Optimized parameters enabled crack-free, fully dense TiAl parts, and post-heat treatments restored a uniform microstructure.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural analysis via optical microscopy and SEM confirmed the absence of cracks and the desired phase distribution.
